finding.requirement: Debit, credit, receipt and exactly one audit row must commit together; failures must leave all unchanged, and replay must execute once.
finding.evidence: Required writes are not checked for affected rows. Reproducer: initialize a temporary database, seed accounts ('t','a',100) and ('t','b',0), then execute CREATE TRIGGER block_write BEFORE INSERT ON audit BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END. Calling transfer(path,'t','a','b',10,'k') returns success. After reopening, balances are 90/10 and a receipt exists, but audit is empty. The CLI also exits 0. The same root cause permits an ignored target UPDATE to leave balances 90/0. Ignoring the transfers INSERT permits an identical replay to debit again, producing balances 80/20, two audit rows and no stored receipt.
finding.suggested_fix: Check that each required UPDATE and INSERT affects exactly one row before committing. Raise a storage exception on any skipped write so the transaction rolls back. Preserve existing triggers and add regression coverage for RAISE(IGNORE).
